findings.description: WorkPoolStatusTriggerFields always binds the status select to name="trigger.expect" regardless of posture. The established pattern in FlowRunStateTriggerFields (lines 21-25) and the new DeploymentStatusTriggerFields (line 31) uses trigger.after for Proactive ("Stays in") and trigger.expect for Reactive ("Enters"), because the backend EventTrigger treats after as the event that must first be seen and expect as the event whose absence fires a Proactive trigger. A Proactive work-pool automation therefore stores the status in expect and fires on the absence of that status event instead of on staying in it; use the posture-dependent field name.
findings.failureMode: Proactive ('Stays in') work-pool status automations fire when the chosen status event does not occur, the opposite of the configured intent.
findings.title: Work pool status ignores Proactive posture field

findings.description: WorkQueueStatusTriggerFields always binds the status select to name="trigger.expect" regardless of posture. FlowRunStateTriggerFields (lines 21-25) and the new DeploymentStatusTriggerFields (line 31) use trigger.after for Proactive ("Stays in") and trigger.expect for Reactive, matching backend EventTrigger semantics where Proactive triggers respond to the absence of expected events after an after event. A Proactive work-queue automation stores the status in expect, so it fires on absence of that status instead of staying in it; use the posture-dependent field name.
findings.failureMode: Proactive ('Stays in') work-queue status automations fire when the chosen status event does not occur, the opposite of the configured intent.
findings.title: Work queue status ignores Proactive posture field

findings.description:
The textarea onChange splits on newlines and calls field.onChange(lines.length > 0 ? lines : undefined), but String.split never returns an empty array: "".split("

findings.failureMode: Submitted custom triggers contain an empty-string expected event that matches no real event and corrupts the trigger's event matching.

findings.description: The diff replaces the deleted line `keyword_like_val = f"%{keyword[:30].encode('unicode_escape').decode('utf-8')}%"` with a plain escape_like_pattern call. findings.description: escape_like_pattern escapes %, _ and backslash with a backslash prefix (api/libs/helper.py:64), but this query declares ESCAPE '|'. findings.failureMode: Full-text fallback search for text containing %, _ or backslash, such as test_data or 50%, matches the wrong documents or misses the literal text.
findings.title: IRIS LIKE search uses ESCAPE '|' for backslash-escaped pattern

findings.description: The Python literal '\\\\' on this line produces two backslash characters in the emitted SQL text, verified by counting the source literal and building the clause. escape_like_pattern escapes wildcards with a single backslash, while SQL ESCAPE requires a single-character escape matching that prefix. The sibling SQLAlchemy call sites all use escape="\\" for a single backslash.
findings.failureMode: Clickzetta fallback LIKE search can fail with an invalid ESCAPE clause or fail to treat \%, \_ and \\ as literals, returning wrong documents for queries containing those characters.
findings.title: Clickzetta LIKE search emits a two-backslash ESCAPE argument

findings.description: The contains, start-with and end-with branches pass escape="\\" to like(), but the not-contains branch calls notlike(f"%{escaped_value}%") with no escape argument. findings.failureMode: A not-contains metadata filter for a value containing % or _, such as 50%, can act as a wildcard exclusion and wrongly exclude documents whose metadata does not literally contain the value.
findings.title: Metadata not-contains filter escapes pattern but omits ESCAPE clause

Repository mandate 2 requires file-scoped namespace declarations in all C# files, and every sibling test file in ServerExecutionTests uses the file-scoped form. Compliance requires restoring 'namespace Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.E2ETests.ServerExecutionTests;' and removing the added braces.
findings.failureMode: The file breaches the mandatory file-scoped namespace rule for C# sources.
findings.title: Block-scoped namespace violates file-scoped rule

findings.description: rewriteClientCommandVector is called with argc=6 but seven robj arguments follow (hsetex, key, KEEPTTL, FIELDS, 1, field, newobj). Its implementation in src/networking.c reads only argc varargs, so newobj is never included and the propagated command is 'HSETEX key KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 field' with no value, which hsetex parsing rejects for wrong number of field/value arguments. Fix by passing argc 7.
findings.failureMode: Replicas and AOF replay receive a malformed HSETEX without the incremented value, so the HINCRBYFLOAT write is lost and replicas diverge from the master.
findings.title: Replicated HSETEX is truncated to 6 args, dropping the value

findings.description: The base code called hashTypeSet with HASH_SET_TAKE_VALUE|HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL, and the integer hincrbyCommand at line 2506 still does. Removing HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL makes hashTypeSet clear any existing field expiry (see the !KEEP_TTL branches at lines 961-963 and 989-992). The PR goal is that the master retains the TTL and the replica must too, so restoring HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL is required.
findings.failureMode: HINCRBYFLOAT on a field with an expiration removes that expiration on the master, leaving the field persistent and inconsistent with a KEEPTTL-preserving replica.
findings.title: Master now clears field TTL by dropping HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL

findings.description: The diff changes 'static GetFieldRes addHashFieldToReply' to a non-static definition. Every caller found by grep is in src/t_hash.c itself and there is no header declaration, so under repository mandate 7 a file-local helper must be declared static. Restore the static keyword.
findings.failureMode: A file-local helper becomes an externally visible symbol, violating the mandated encapsulation rule and polluting the global symbol table.
findings.title: Internal helper addHashFieldToReply loses static linkage

findings.description: The diff deletes DownloadToast's nested `UX` struct (`static let buttonSize: CGFloat = 40`) and replaces both uses with the literal `40` at lines 192-193. Repository mandate 13 requires UI layout constants to live in a nested UX struct and names scattered literals as the failure mode; grep confirms no other UX constant now supplies this size. Compliance requires restoring the UX struct (e.g. `private struct UX { static let buttonSize: CGFloat = 40 }`) and referencing `UX.buttonSize` at both constraint sites.
findings.failureMode: The close-button size becomes an unorganized magic number duplicated at two sites, violating the mandated UX-struct rule and allowing the height and width to drift apart on future edits.
findings.title: DownloadToast inlines button-size literals after deleting its UX struct

findings.description: handleShowReaderModeAction in BrowserViewControllerState now returns displayView .readerModeLongPressAction instead of base .readerMode (git diff vs base). In BrowserViewController.handleDisplayActions, .readerMode calls toggleReaderMode() while .readerModeLongPressAction calls toggleReaderModeLongPressAction(), which adds the page to the reading list; the identical .readerModeLongPressAction in handleAddToReadingListLongPressAction (line 590) confirms this is the long-press path copied into the tap path. Restore displayView: .readerMode.
findings.failureMode: Tapping the reader mode toolbar button adds the page to the reading list with a toast instead of enabling/disabling Reader Mode.
findings.title: Reader-mode tap now triggers reading-list long-press action

findings.description: Base code kept the tab URL only when (isWebPage() && !isReaderModeURL); the change flips this to (isWebPage() || isReaderModeURL). isReaderModeURL is http://localhost/reader-mode/page (URLExtension.swift:313-316), so reader-mode URLs previously became nil and now pass through into ToolbarAction.cancelEdit, where AddressBarState.handleCancelEditAction adopts action.url over the state.url fallback. Restore the && !isReaderModeURL condition.
findings.failureMode: Cancelling edit mode (e.g. via tabs/menu) on a Reader Mode page puts the internal localhost reader-mode URL into address bar state instead of retaining the page URL.
findings.title: cancelEditMode now keeps internal reader-mode URLs

findings.description: recordReaderModeTelemetry swapped the base mapping: .available now yields false and default yields true, contradicting the retained comment 'will be enabled after action gets executed'. ReaderModeState.available means reader mode can be turned on by this tap, so the isEnabled argument passed to toolbarTelemetry.readerModeButtonTapped is inverted for every tap. Restore .available: true, default: false.
findings.failureMode: Every reader_mode_button_tapped event records the opposite enabled state, corrupting Reader Mode telemetry.
findings.title: Reader-mode telemetry enabled flag inverted

findings.description: The diff changes 'private let gleanWrapper' to internal 'let gleanWrapper' with no caller needing the wider access (grep shows only initializer injection and internal use). This breaks AGENTS.md rule 11, which requires implementation-detail properties to be private. Restore the private modifier.
findings.failureMode: An internal telemetry dependency is exposed module-wide in breach of the repository access-control mandate.
findings.title: ToolbarTelemetry gleanWrapper access control widened

findings.description: The rename changed pageActionStack.arrangedSubviews to a duplicate browserActionStack.arrangedSubviews, omitting trailingPageActionStack from stacks. updateActionStack sets alpha=0 on newly added buttons and updateToolbarLayout is the code that restores alpha=1.0, so newly added trailing page-action buttons are never restored. Fix: use trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews.
findings.failureMode: Trailing page-action buttons in the address toolbar remain invisible (alpha 0) after configure.
findings.title: Trailing page actions never fade in

findings.description: Base code pinned toolbar.leading to leftSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor (container leading) and trailing to rightSkeletonAddressBar.leadingAnchor (container trailing). The change pins leading to rightSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor, which is off-screen to the right of the container (right skeleton leading=container trailing, width≈container width), making leading > trailing. Fix: restore leftSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor.
findings.failureMode: With swiping tabs enabled, toolbar constraints are unsatisfiable/inverted and the address toolbar is collapsed or off-screen.
findings.title: Toolbar leading pinned to right skeleton bar

findings.description: Base code used pageActionStack (now trailingPageActionStack) to decide dividerWidthConstraint, but the change reads leadingPageActionStack. The divider sits between locationView and trailingPageActionStack (lines 268-272), so its width must follow the trailing stack. Fix: check trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews.isEmpty.
findings.failureMode: Divider is missing when only trailing actions exist and appears spuriously when only leading actions exist.
findings.title: Divider width keyed to wrong page-action stack

findings.description: isLandscape is assigned from the deprecated UIApplication.shared.statusBarOrientation and never read anywhere in the file (only occurrence besides the .isLandscape property). The comment claims landscape layout adjustments that do not exist. Fix: remove the variable and comment.
findings.failureMode: Compiler produces an unused-variable (and deprecation) warning and the dead call gives no layout effect.
findings.title: Unused isLandscape variable added

findings.description: Line 177 changes config.get("identifier") to config.get("bundle") and then calls as_str() on it. In tauri.conf.json the top-level identifier is a string while bundle is an object (config.schema.json), so as_str() always returns None and original_identifier is always None. Mobile callers in crates/tauri-cli/src/mobile/mod.rs:395 and :412 then fail with 'app configuration is missing an identifier' even for valid configs; the fix is to restore reading the top-level "identifier" key.
findings.failureMode: Mobile dev/build flows abort claiming a missing identifier for every valid tauri.conf.json.
findings.title: original_identifier reads bundle object as string

findings.description: Line 202 changes the guard from extension == "json" || extension == "json5" to using && between the two comparisons. A path has a single extension, so the condition can never be true and config_schema_validator().iter_errors() is never reached. Invalid tauri.conf.json/json5 files that previously logged schema errors and exited with exit(1) are now silently accepted; the fix is to restore ||.
findings.failureMode: Schema validation of tauri.conf.json never runs, so invalid configs pass without the required errors or exit.
findings.title: Impossible extension condition disables schema validation

findings.description: Line 289 replaces the deleted line `config_metadata.inner = serde_json::from_value(value).context("failed to parse config")?;` with an extensions.insert() call, so the merged `value` computed on lines 286-288 is dropped and config_metadata.inner is never updated. Callers in xcode_script.rs:145 and android_studio_script.rs:98 merge --config overrides and then read the config handle (for example build.dev_url), so they observe the stale pre-merge configuration. The fix is to restore assigning the deserialized merged value to config_metadata.inner.
findings.failureMode: --config overrides passed to the mobile studio scripts have no effect on the loaded configuration.
findings.title: merge_with discards the merged config value

findings.description: Line 153 is a 156-character statement that rustfmt rewraps onto two lines, verified by running rustfmt --check on this file, which reports a diff at this line. AGENTS.md rule 3 requires all Rust code to pass 'cargo fmt --all -- --check' with the project rustfmt configuration (max_width=100). Compliance requires wrapping the serde_json::from_str call before .expect(...).
findings.failureMode: The mandated cargo fmt --check gate fails on this file.
findings.title: New validator line violates rustfmt (AGENTS.md rule 3)

findings.description: The atoms Biome override now bans `@calcom/trpc/**`, but two unchanged atoms files still import `QueryCell` from `@calcom/trpc/components/QueryCell`: `connect/conferencing-apps/ConferencingAppsViewPlatformWrapper.tsx:12` and `selected-calendars/wrappers/SelectedCalendarsSettingsPlatformWrapper.tsx:6`, verified by grep at head. Both match the override includes pattern `packages/platform/atoms/**/*.{ts,tsx,...}` with level `error`, so `biome lint --error-on-warnings` now fails on this package. The ban must be accompanied by removing or relocating those imports.
findings.failureMode: Biome lint errors on the two remaining @calcom/trpc/components/QueryCell imports, failing CI/pre-commit for the atoms package.
findings.title: Widened @calcom/trpc ban breaks remaining QueryCell imports in atoms

findings.description: The original `GetAvailableSlotsResponse` derives from `IGetAvailableSlots` in trpc slots util, whose `fromUser` is `IFromUser` with `id: number` (getUserAvailability.ts:177). The new local copy declares `id: string`. `EventTypeCalendarViewComponent` passes `useAvailableSlots` data to `useAvailableTimeSlots`, which expects `IGetAvailableSlots`, so the string id is not assignable to the numeric id and atoms typechecking fails.
findings.failureMode: TypeScript rejects assigning the new GetAvailableSlotsResponse to IGetAvailableSlots in the calendar view, breaking the atoms build.
findings.title: SlotInfo.fromUser.id changed from number to string

findings.description: Prisma `Availability.days` is `Int[]` and the original list handler returns `availability: true`, so days are numbers; `getScheduleListItemData` likewise declares `days: number[]`. The new `GetAvailabilityListHandlerReturn` declares `days: string[]`. `ListSchedulesPlatformWrapper` passes these schedules to `getScheduleListItemData(schedule)`, so the new type is not assignable and atoms typechecking fails.
findings.failureMode: TypeScript rejects passing useAtomGetAllSchedules data to getScheduleListItemData, breaking the ListSchedules atom build.
findings.title: Availability days typed as string[] instead of number[]

findings.description: The deleted trpc definition declared `userIds?: number[]`, matching slot producers such as `TimeFrame.userIds?: number[]` in features/schedules/lib/slots.ts. The moved copy in booker/types.ts declares `string[]`. Consumers of the public `onTimeslotsLoaded` prop, typed with this `Slot`, are now told ids are strings while runtime slot userIds are numeric user ids.
findings.failureMode: Consumers typed against Slot.userIds as string[] receive numeric ids at runtime, causing type errors or wrong string handling of user ids.
findings.title: Slot.userIds changed from number[] to string[]

findings.description: The new validator only checks that input is an object and `name` is a non-empty string, then returns `data as CreateScheduleInput`. It never validates `schedule` (must be `{start: Date; end: Date}[][]` per the original ZCreateInputSchema) or `eventTypeId` (must be a number). Input such as `{name: 'x', schedule: 'bad', eventTypeId: '1'}` passes validation and is handed on with a trusted CreateScheduleInput type.
findings.failureMode: Malformed schedule/eventTypeId values pass validation and reach schedule creation with a trusted type, causing runtime errors or invalid API payloads.
findings.title: validateCreateScheduleInput returns unchecked schedule and eventTypeId

findings.description: Repository rule 10 requires custom error classes extending base types (HttpError, CalendarAppError, ErrorWithCode) with typed codes, and lists throwing generic Error objects as a failure. The new validator throws `new Error(...)` here and again at line 46, giving callers no typed code or structured context to branch on. Compliance requires a typed error such as ErrorWithCode.
findings.failureMode: Validation failures surface as untyped generic errors that callers cannot categorise by code, violating the repository error-handling mandate.
findings.title: Generic Error throws violate typed error rule

findings.description: Biome is configured with javascript formatter `quoteStyle: "double"` (biome.json:58) and repository rule 3 mandates the standardised Biome formatting. The new validator uses single-quoted strings on lines 39, 40, 45 and 46. A Biome format check rewrites or flags every one of these lines.
findings.failureMode: The new file fails Biome formatting checks, blocking lint-staged/format CI gates until reformatted to double quotes.
findings.title: Single quotes violate Biome double-quote formatting

findings.description: The controller uses @Roles("TEAM_MEMBER") instead of TEAM_ADMIN. I verified RolesGuard/hasMinimumRole with TEAM_ROLES=[TEAM_OWNER,TEAM_ADMIN,TEAM_MEMBER]: TEAM_MEMBER is the lowest minimum, so a membership with role MEMBER passes. This contradicts the PR contract (Requires TEAM_ADMIN), the parallel organizations invite controller's @Roles("TEAM_ADMIN"), and the new e2e test expecting 403 for a non-admin member. Fix: use @Roles("TEAM_ADMIN").
findings.failureMode: Any regular team member can create a shareable team invite link, an authorization bypass that lets outsiders join the team.
findings.title: Invite endpoint allows regular team members, not only admins

findings.description: The new-token branch returns token: newToken.identifier, where identifier was just set to the deterministic string `invite-link-for-teamId-${teamId}` (line 90), while inviteLink is built from the random token. The base code returned the random token, and the existing-token branch returns existingToken.token. Fix: return newToken.token (or token).
findings.failureMode: Every new invite returns a predictable non-token value that differs from the token in inviteLink and is identical across requests, breaking token consumers and the e2e assertions that inviteLink contains token and tokens rotate.
findings.title: createInvite returns identifier instead of the generated token

findings.description: The condition changed from base `if (!isOrgContext) return teamInviteLink` to `if (isOrgContext) return teamInviteLink`. Base behaviour (and the variable name orgInviteLink for the /signup branch) routes regular teams to /teams?token= and organization/org-team invites to /signup?token=&callbackUrl=getting-started; the new code swaps both. Fix: restore `if (!isOrgContext)`. This also affects existing callers (tRPC createInvite handler and the organizations invite controller), not only the new endpoint.
findings.failureMode: Regular-team invitees are sent through the org signup/getting-started flow and organization invitees to /teams, producing wrong invite links on the mainline invite path.
findings.title: buildInviteLink org/team routing inverted
